title: Hearsay and guesses: そう, そうだ, そうです
summary: そう after the stem of a word means "looks like"; そうだ after a whole sentence means "I heard that". Two different jobs that look alike.

blocks.text: **そう** belongs to the family こう, そう, ああ, どう (lesson 20): it means "that way". From that it grows two jobs, and the trick is to know which one you are looking at.
Here **そう** is attached to a **single word** and makes an adjectival noun. How the word is trimmed depends on its engine:

rows: 降りそう (looks about to fall)

blocks.text: Plain nouns cannot take this そう. Japanese is careful about what you claim: you can only say おいしい after tasting, but おいしそう from the look of it.

blocks.jp: このケーキはおいしそうだ。
空が暗くて、雨が降りそうだ。
blocks.en: The sky is dark and it looks like rain.

blocks.jp: 静かそうな女の子が来た。

blocks.text: Here **そうだ / そうです** is **not** a suffix. It attaches to a **whole sentence** in its plain form, and that sentence becomes the content of what you heard. The sentence itself keeps its own tense.

blocks.jp: 先生は来週戻るそうだ。
blocks.en: I hear the teacher will be back next week.

blocks.jp: さくらは日本人だそうだ。
blocks.en: I have heard that Sakura is Japanese.

items: **Stem + そう** = looks like (appearance); no noun allowed.
**Plain sentence + そうだ** = I heard that (hearsay).
い-adjective: drop **い**; verb: use the **い-stem**; adjectival noun: drop **だ / な**.
降りそう (about to rain) and 降るそう (I hear it rains) are different.

questions.note: い-adjective: drop い, add そう.
Adjectival noun: drop だ / な.
Verb: い-stem + そう.
Drop the い of 難しい before そう.

questions.prompt: このかばんはじょうぶ＿＿だ。
questions.note: Adjectival noun: drop だ / な, add そう.

questions.instruction: Which says "I heard that it will snow"?
questions.note: Plain sentence + そうだ is hearsay.

questions.instruction: Which says "The cup looks like it will fall"?
options: コップが落ちるそうだ
コップが落ちたそうだ
questions.note: い-stem + そうだ: it looks about to happen.

questions.instruction: Which can NOT take the "looks like" そう?
options: 降り (the stem of 降る)
questions.note: Plain nouns cannot take appearance そう.

questions.instruction: Which says "I heard that my friend came yesterday"?
options: 友達は昨日来るそうだ
友達は昨日来たそうだ
友達は昨日来たそうに
questions.note: Past plain form + そうだ: the sentence keeps its own tense.

questions.prompt: あの店は人が多＿＿ですね。
questions.note: 多い: drop い, add そう.
questions.en: That shop looks crowded, doesn't it?

questions.note: Plain sentence + そうだ: 病気だ keeps its だ.
questions.en: I hear Mr. Tanaka is ill.

questions.prompt: 友達は来月結婚するそうだ。
questions.note: A whole plain sentence + そうだ: hearsay.
questions.en: I hear my friend is getting married next month.

questions.note: そうな before a noun.

questions.prompt: The "looks like" ending can follow a plain noun such as "student".
questions.note: Plain nouns need another word, such as らしい or ようだ.

questions.prompt: The two kinds of そう in this lesson mean the same thing.
questions.note: One is how it looks, the other is I heard.
Ichidan verb: drop る, add そう.
い-adjective: drop い, add そうだ.
